figures.name: Thagyamin

ability.name: New Year Blessing
ability.description: Reset all cooldowns for allied cards; begin a new cycle with fresh abilities.

figures.description: The king of the nats and lord of the heavens in Burmese belief, who descends to earth during Thingyan New Year to record the deeds of humans.

figures.name: Shwe Pyin Gyi

ability.name: Brother Smith Rage
ability.description: Deal 8 damage to one enemy; if this kills them, deal 4 splash to adjacent cards.

figures.description: The older of the two blacksmith-nat brothers, fierce and impulsive, whose violent death created a powerful nat spirit.

figures.name: Shwe Pyin Nge

ability.name: Brother's Plan
ability.description: Formulate an ambush; the next attack by any allied card deals double damage.

figures.description: The younger of the two blacksmith nat brothers, cunning and clever, who together with his brother form one of the most feared nat pairs.

figures.name: Lady Golden Face (Shwe Myet Hna)

ability.name: Golden Jealousy
ability.description: Cause one enemy card to attack another enemy card instead of you.

figures.description: A beautiful nat spirit associated with love and jealousy, one of the thirty-seven official nats of Burma, said to cause discord between lovers.

figures.name: Ma Ngwe Taung

ability.name: Mountain Purity
ability.description: Purify one allied card; remove all debuffs and restore 4 HP.

figures.description: The silver mountain nat spirit who presides over highland purification rituals, associated with the Shan hills and mountain shrines.

figures.name: Maung Po Tu

ability.name: Tiger Form
ability.description: Transform into a tiger temporarily; gain +3 power and speed for 2 turns.

figures.description: A nat spirit associated with tigers who guards the forest, propitiated by hunters and those who venture into the wilderness.

figures.name: Min Mahagiri

ability.name: Home Guardian
ability.description: Protect one allied structure or card permanently; it cannot be targeted until destroyed.

figures.description: The Lord of the Great Mountain, a house-protecting nat and one of the most important in the pantheon, associated with Mount Popa.

figures.name: Hnamadawgyi

ability.name: Royal Court
ability.description: Grant all royalty-domain allied cards +2 to all stats for 2 turns.

figures.description: A royal female nat spirit of the court, one of the official 37 nats who protects those of noble bearing.

figures.name: Aung Pinle Hsinbyuyin

ability.name: White Elephant Blessing
ability.description: Grant the most powerful allied card immunity to all attacks for 1 turn.

figures.description: The nat of the white elephant, most auspicious of animals in Burmese tradition, associated with royal power and cosmic blessing.

figures.name: Lady Three Times Beautiful

ability.name: Triple Beauty
ability.description: Charm three enemy cards simultaneously; they cannot attack for 1 turn.

figures.description: One of the thirty-seven official nats, celebrated for her triple beauty, associated with dance and feminine power.

figures.name: Popa Medaw

ability.name: Flower Power
ability.description: All nature-domain allies gain +3 to magic; all fire-domain enemies lose 3.

figures.description: The Mother Spirit of Mount Popa, originally a flower-eating ogress who became the surrogate mother of the blacksmith nat brothers, ruling from the sacred volcano.

figures.name: Zawgyi

ability.name: Elixir of Youth
ability.description: Grant immortality to one allied card for 2 turns; they cannot be destroyed.

figures.description: The red-clad Burmese alchemist who achieved immortality through mystical elixirs, flying through the air and obsessively seeking the red flower of immortality.

figures.name: Weizza

ability.name: Occult Knowledge
ability.description: Look at the top 5 cards of any deck; rearrange them in any order.

figures.description: The weizza, spiritually advanced beings who have achieved near-immortality through occult practices, expected to help the future Buddha.

figures.name: Manuha

ability.name: King in Chains
ability.description: Even in defeat, inspire all allied cards; they gain +2 wisdom and refuse to flee.

figures.description: The Mon king kept captive in Pagan, who built the cramped Buddha statues to express his own feelings of constriction, a symbol of dignified resistance.

figures.name: Shin Arahan

ability.name: Dharma Reform
ability.description: Convert one dark-aligned card to neutral; they gain 3 wisdom and lose dark powers.

figures.description: The Mon monk who converted King Anawrahta to Theravada Buddhism, transforming the Burmese kingdom and establishing the dominant religious tradition.

figures.name: Anawrahta

ability.name: Pagan Unification
ability.description: Unite all allied cards under one banner; all gain +2 to all stats permanently.

figures.description: The founder of the Pagan Empire and first king of unified Burma, who conquered the Mon and established Theravada Buddhism throughout his kingdom.

figures.name: Naga (Burmese)

ability.name: Rain Serpent
ability.description: Summon rain; all plant-domain allies gain 3 HP while fire-domain enemies lose 3 HP.

figures.description: The great water serpent spirits of Burmese belief, who control rain and water, propitiated to ensure good harvests.

figures.name: Yama (Burma)

ability.name: Final Judgment
ability.description: Judge one card's entire history; deal damage equal to their total transgressions.

figures.description: The lord of the dead and judgment in Burmese Buddhist cosmology, who weighs the deeds of souls and assigns their next realm of rebirth.

figures.name: Thurathati (Saraswati)

ability.name: Divine Learning
ability.description: Grant one allied card +3 wisdom and the ability to copy any one ability seen.

figures.description: The Burmese form of Saraswati, goddess of learning, arts, and wisdom, patron of students and scholars throughout Burma.

figures.name: Galon (Burmese Garuda)

ability.name: Serpent Hunt
ability.description: Hunt all naga-type enemies; deal 7 damage to each naga card on the field.

figures.description: The divine eagle-man of Burmese tradition, eternal enemy of the nagas, symbol of solar power and later adopted as the emblem of resistance.
